lesson_title: The Rigged Shop and the Bank Account Under Your Feet
hook_text: Imagine a shop where your trolley buys less every single year — same money, same goods. Whole countries shop there.
clip_script: Why do some countries stay poor? Imagine a shop whose rules were written before you walked in. You are permitted to sell only raw things — ore, beans, crude — and required to buy back finished things — phones, machines, medicine. Raw prices wobble and sag; finished prices climb steadily. Each year your trolley of ore buys a little less than the year before — that sliding ratio is the terms of trade, and it is the trap built into the old colonial pattern: the wealth pools wherever the making happens. The escape is to start making — beneficiation, turning your own gold into jewellery and your own chrome into stainless steel, climbing the value chain exactly as East Asia climbed from cheap factories to rich economies. And the same shop operates inside the country: Gauteng is South Africa's own core, making and banking, while the former homeland regions supply labour and receive remittances — one rigged shop, running at two scales. Underneath all of it sits a bank account: topsoil, filling at a teaspoon a year and emptying by the bucket in a single storm on bare ground. Soil is capital and the harvest its interest — erosion is spending capital and booking it as income. That is the whole year in one rule: live off the interest, never touch the capital.
visual_style: A sketched shop counter where a trolley of ore shrinks year by year against a rising shelf of phones and machines; a golden value-chain ladder from ore to jewellery; a split map of core and periphery pulsing with labour and remittance arrows; a bank book stamped TOPSOIL filling by teaspoons and draining by buckets.
mood: Sharp-eyed and empowering — the rules exposed, then the way out drawn.
pacing: Cool deliberate build through the shop's rules, a lift at the escape ladder, a grounded landing on the bank-account rule.
call_to_action: Watch the full revision session and walk the circle that joins the whole year.
